summary: Iteration 17 — Trip-wise Diesel-from-Customer & Cash-Advance deductions on Invoice. Verified backend end-to-end (6/6 pytest passed) and frontend (InvoiceView + InvoiceCreate preview). Formula Net Freight = Freight + Halting + Excess − Shortage − Diesel-from-Customer − Customer-Advance is honoured everywhere: _trip_billable, create_invoice, _recompute_invoice on trip edit, PDF (labels 'Less: Diesel from Customer', 'Less: Customer Advance Received', 'Net Freight (Taxable)' + per-trip sub-rows), InvoiceView.jsx (per-trip sub-rows + summary rows + Net Freight label), InvoiceCreate.jsx preview (dieselDedTotal + advanceDedTotal + Net Freight (Taxable)). Multi-company scoping regression clean — C2 preview does not see C1 trips; cross-company invoice creation rejected (400). Regression: trips without diesel/advance produce zero deductions.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py _trip_billable() at L732-733 subtracts BOTH t.shortage_amount AND (expenses.shortage_amount). If a user ever populates both fields the shortage will be double-counted. Trip model exposes shortage_amount at both the trip level (auto-computed from shortage_qty × product_rate_per_mt) and inside Expenses. Recommend picking one canonical field or explicitly documenting/zeroing the other. Not in scope for iter17 but worth cleaning up.

PUT /api/trips/{tid} requires a full Trip body (Pydantic v2 strict). Any client sending a partial patch will get a 422. The current React UI always resends the whole trip so this is fine, but consider adding PATCH semantics or accepting Optional fields to make edits safer from scripts/imports.
There is no GET /api/trips/{tid} endpoint — only list. Not blocking (frontend loads via list + filter), but individual-trip fetch would be useful for deep-linking and testability.
invoice creation path recomputes subtotal / diesel_deduction_total / advance_deduction_total identically to _recompute_invoice — could DRY into one helper to prevent drift.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (InvoiceView + InvoiceCreate preview both verified visually and via DOM assertions)

Multi-company scoping unaffected. Note server.py has a latent shortage-double-count bug when both t.shortage_amount and expenses.shortage_amount are set — not exercised by this iteration but flagged for cleanup.
